units_check: x 4960..28000 = 620..3500 rpm; y 0..2061 = 0..140 mm3; grid 19x16, 0..177 counts = 0..12.0 mm3 (plateaus 22 and 29 counts = 1.5 and 2.0 mm3 for 10..65 mm3 demand at 1000..2000 rpm, top corner 177 counts = 12.0 mm3 at 140 mm3 and 2900 rpm; round at 0.0679 mm3 per count, whereas as 0.1171875 deg timing counts 22 / 29 / 177 would be 2.6 / 3.4 / 20.7 deg); 61 non-zero cells
evidence: Output chain: crank_sync_threshold is read only by cm848_fuel_demand_state_capture (copy to RAM 0x3fd080); engine_injectionAngle_updateCutoutAndTimingDemand scales it by injection_timing_demand_working / 0xc800 exactly like the fuel quantity snapshots and uses it as the cap of engine_timing_delta; engine_timing_delta is subtracted from the per-bank quantity accumulators engine_timing_reference_high / _low (cm848_calculateEngineTimingInterpolation) and turned into a pulse width by post_injection_pulse_width_* with the auxiliary timing offset cam_sync_period_reference_b (cm848_calculateEngineFaultTiming). Axes are word-identical (compared) to injection_timing_auxiliary_base_map of the sibling cm848_auxiliary_boundary_condition_eval, with the same base-map role in cm848_filterInputValue and the same call flags (4); what differs is the clamps of the function: 0..0x1700 on candidate 4 and 0..0xffff on the result, against +-0x400 in the timing sibling (signed timing angles).
naming_concern: The whole destination chain is misnamed: injection_timing_boost_blend, injection_timing_demand_cyl6, injection_timing_factor_cyl6_a / _b, governor_fuel_demand_limit_lo / _hi, crank_rpm_calc_factor_a / _b, crank_sync_threshold, crank_sync_state_counter, injection_timing_arb_source_packed and the function cm848_calculateGovernorOutput are the auxiliary (post-main) injection QUANTITY limit, not timing, governor or crank sync; post_injection_pulse_width_* is the same injection under the word post (unify auxiliary vs post in a later pass).
